 Wisconsin DMV explains how to obtain an ID for voting
 October 26, 2026 by Daily Dodge 
 MADISON — Wisconsin residents who do not already have an approved form of identification can obtain a state ID to use at the polls, according to the Wisconsin Department of Transportation Division of Motor Vehicles.
 Wisconsin voters are required to show identification when casting a ballot, but there is no separate “voter ID.” A federally compliant REAL ID also is not required for voting.
 Voters can check the Wisconsin Elections Commission website at bringit.wi.gov to review the forms of identification accepted at polling places.
 Residents applying for their first Wisconsin identification card should visit wisconsindmv.gov/idcards to review the required documents. Applicants can then visit their nearest DMV Customer Service Center. Appointments are available but not required.
 U.S. citizens can obtain an identification card free of charge. If the card is not available before an election, the DMV can provide a receipt that is valid for voting.
 Questions about obtaining an ID can be directed to the DMV’s toll-free hotline at 844-588-1069.
 Questions about voter eligibility, polling locations, voter registration or other election information should be directed to the Wisconsin Elections Commission at elections.wi.gov .
